messages:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT ALERT: decode-gpu pool experiencing repeated CUDA OOMs across 3 nodes, triggered at 2026-02-11T09:00:34Z. Pager notified: Ryan (oncall).
Ryan (oncall): ack — pulling logs and attaching to thread. what's the customer impact so far?
Sam (eng-runtime): i'm seeing node-42, node-47, node-51 throwing `CUDA out of memory` in decode loop, memory spike correlates with long generation requests. stack shows `llama_decode_loop()` -> `kv_cache.grow()` -> cudaMalloc fail.
Anya (ml-infra): tagging metrics: GPU mem usage jumped from 8GB->24GB within 4s on those nodes, and the scheduler queue spiked.
Leo (support): reported customer: acme-marketing experiencing ~70% request drops to streaming endpoints, some 5xxs. ticket #C-4832.
Ryan (oncall): temp mitigation: can we isolate offending clients and throttle? any quick config to drop huge max_tokens?
Sam (eng-runtime): we can enable server-side enforcement of `max_output_tokens` per-route, but current deployment relies on client-sent header `x-max-tokens` and we only validate <= model.max_context. looks like a client is sending 20000.
Anya (ml-infra): deploy autoscaler paused because OOMs cause failures; nodes are flapping. prefer to quarantine clients so other traffic continues.
OpsBot: quarantine action recommended: add ip-level rate-limits + reject requests with >4096 tokens. run `rbctl route update --max-output 4096 --enforce`?
Sam (eng-runtime): making small patch to runtime to reject extreme `max_tokens` earlier in the request pipeline, will push a hot-config via kill-switch route in ~2 min.
Ryan (oncall): proceed. also can we fallback affected routes to smaller model to reduce per-token memory?
Sam (eng-runtime): yes — plan: route heavy streaming requests to quantized 8-bit variant (gptx-quant-oct) with lower KV growth. Will do Canary rollout on two nodes.
Maya (customer-ops): looping in ACME CSM to give ETA to customer; need actionable ETA and whether requests will be retried.
Leo (support): note to ticket: "We are actively mitigating; temporary reduced capacity and retries may occur. Will update shortly."
Sam (eng-runtime): hot-config applied: `--enforce-max-output=4096` rolled to the cluster coordinator. monitoring.
Anya (ml-infra): immediately after enforcement, node OOM rate dropped by 85% on green nodes. still seeing OOMs on node-51 where the process is stuck.
Ryan (oncall): node-51 logs? paste tail.
Sam (eng-runtime): ```
2026-02-11T09:03:12Z ERROR decode_loop: CUDA error: out of memory during kv_cache.expand
2026-02-11T09:03:13Z WARN watchdog: healthcheck failing, restarting process
2026-02-11T09:03:14Z INFO container: restarting container
2026-02-11T09:03:15Z ERROR container: crashloop: exit code 137
```
Anya (ml-infra): restarting the instance kernel + docker reset; will keep the node cordoned until stable.
OpsBot: action recorded: cordon node-51; start replacement node-63 with fresh GPU.
Ryan (oncall): any evidence this was triggered by a single customer session? or widespread malformed headers?
Sam (eng-runtime): logs show a batch of requests from IP 18.129.45.22 with header `x-max-tokens: 20000` and `content-length` consistent with short prompts — indicates a misconfigured client-side max_tokens not actual content size. we dropped those post-enforce but some prior requests caused OOM.
Leo (support): reaching out to ACME: they use our SDK v0.9.2 — I'll confirm whether their integration overrides server caps.
Maya (customer-ops): ACME engineering replied: they had a regression in our sample app that set `max_tokens: 20000` when using streaming. they're rolling a fix.
Sam (eng-runtime): post-enforce (#1) metrics: token throughput is back to ~92% baseline, error rate down from 18%->3%. request drop window is roughly 3m (peak) while node restarts and canaries finish.
Ryan (oncall): good. next: permanent prevention. propose changes: server-side hard cap, validation in load-balancer, and telemetry alert on per-client max_tokens anomalies.
Anya (ml-infra): agree. also suggest autoscaler safety: don't schedule large decode jobs onto nodes with < X% free GPU mem to avoid immediate OOM.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR with runtime validation + reject response code 422 on invalid max_tokens, and a fallback policy to route heavy streams to quantized model.
Ryan (oncall): will you add a transient mitigation runbook entry for oncall? include quick commands: `rbctl route update --max-output`, `kubectl cordon node-XX`, `rbctl isolate-client --ip X.X.X.X`.
Sam (eng-runtime): done — created runbook section and linked to infra playbook. PR #2389.
Maya (customer-ops): ACME wants an ETA for full resolution and root cause summary. timeline?
Leo (support): telling ACME: hotfix and caps applied; we expect full recovery in 45-60 minutes while canaries finish and we bring replacement nodes online.
Ryan (oncall): monitoring for any residual OOMs. if we see repeat, escalate to SEV.
Anya (ml-infra): node-51 is back after replacement node-63 ready; cordon cleared. health checks green.
Sam (eng-runtime): canary to quantized model successful; rolling to remaining nodes now.
IncidentBot: UPDATE: incident severity downgraded to P2 at 2026-02-11T09:28:07Z; customer-facing impact reduced.
Maya (customer-ops): ACME confirmed degraded requests stopped after 09:22 UTC. they asked if we can block the misconfigured SDK versions from contacting prod.
Sam (eng-runtime): we'll add a warning and block rule for SDK v0.9.2 that sets >4096 by default. ops will drop their requests at edge.
Ryan (oncall): handoff: i'll document timeline and leave in postmortem queue. Sam, please capture the exact request logs and the patch details. Anya, capture autoscaler threshold change. Leo/Maya, coordinate final customer note.
Sam (eng-runtime): will add logs and annotated diffs to PR.
Anya (ml-infra): will add config changes to infra repo and a metric alert: `alert: ClientMaxTokensHigh` when >100 requests/min with client max_tokens > 4096.
Leo (support): final customer note prepared: "Root cause: client misconfiguration sent excessive max_tokens causing KV growth and CUDA OOMs; mitigation: server-side cap and model routing; follow-up: SDK block & patch guidance." sending now.
Maya (customer-ops): ACME notified and satisfied with remediation. closing on-customer impact.
Ryan (oncall): closing incident thread. follow-ups: postmortem draft (owners: Sam/Anya/Leo) and timelines. thanks all. :thumbsup:
